articleTitle: On evaluation of the confluent Heun functions
abstract: In this paper we consider the confluent Heun equation, which is a linear differential equation of second order with three singular points (two regular and one irregular). A procedure for numerical evaluation of the equation's solutions (confluent Heun functions) is proposed. The scheme is based on power series, asymptotic expansions and analytic continuation. Results of numerical tests are given.

articleTitle: Equations for velocity oscillations in problems of a fluid flow along a plate with small periodic irregularities on the surface for large Reynolds numbers
abstract: Depending on the scales of periodic irregularities in the problem under study, a solution arises which describes two ("double-deck") or three ("triple-deck") boundary layers on the plate. Mainly, we study the equations describing the velocity oscillations in the boundary layers arising because of periodic irregularities and show their command nature.

articleTitle: Harmonic waves in the simplest reduced Kelvin’s and gyrostatic media under an external body follower torque
abstract: We consider two types of homogeneous reduced elastic media with finite dynamic spin. One is Kelvin's medium, whose particles have axial symmetry and may freely rotate about their axes. Its equations are analogous to those of ferromagnetic insulators near the state of magnetic saturation. Another one is a gyrostatic medium, consisting of spherical body-points containing rotors. Gyroscopic term prevails in the dynamics of both continua. Axes in the reference configuration are collinear. We consider reduced media, whose elastic energy does not depend on the gradient of turn, under the follower body torque, proportional to the rotational displacement. We obtain that there exist polarised shear harmonic waves. The only exception is for the wave vector orthogonal to the axes: in this case we have two shear plane waves, one has a band gap and another one is classical. For the direction of wave propagation parallel to the unit vector, polarisation is circular and does not depend on frequency. In all other cases, polarisation is elliptic and depends on the frequency and on the direction of the wave propagation relatively to the axes. If the external follower torque is positive (reduces the rotational displacement of the body-point), one of the polarised waves has a band gap and another one not. Changing the external loading, we change the band gap. If we apply a negative torque, depending on the direction of the wave propagation and parameters we may obtain band gaps for both branches and a decreasing part of dispersion curve for one of them just above the cut-off frequency. Thus this media behave as smart acoustic metamaterials, single or double negative, depending on the wave polarisation, external torque, parameters and the frequency domain.

articleTitle: Analysis of a mathematical model of oxygen transport in brain
abstract: A continuum two-compartment model of oxygen transport in brain is studied. The model comprises two coupled, highly nonlinear partial differential equations describing the oxygen concentration in the blood and tissue compartments. A priori estimates of solutions are obtained, and a simple iteration procedure for finding them is proposed. The convergence of this method is proven. A numerical example illustrates the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Generalized Chebychev polynomials connected with a point interaction for the discrete Schrödinger equation
abstract: We consider a semi-infinite Jacobi matrix corresponding to a point interaction for the discrete Schrödinger operator. The entries of this matrix with indices (i, i - 1) and (i - 1, i) are equal to 1 if i ≠ k or to some positive number a if i = k. All other entries of this matrix are equal to zero. The spectral analysis of this problem (for k = 1) leads to a new class of polynomials generalizing the classical Chebyshev polynomials [1]. We will extend this class from the case k = 1 to the case of any integer k ≥ 1. Namely, we find for these polynomials expressions in terms of the classical Chebyshev polynomials. We obtain also a measure of orthogonality for generalized Chebyshev polynomials. This report is a continuation of authors' work [2].

articleTitle: Backwards waves in a fluid-filled cylindrical shell: comparison of 2D shell theories with 3D theory of elasticity
abstract: Backward waves (wave with opposite signs of the phase and group velocities) in a circular cylindrical shell filled with an acoustic fluid are studied. Three theories are applied to describe the motions of the shell: Kirchhoff-Love theory, refined shell theory with modified inertia, and 3D theory of elasticity. Numerical results for combinations of parameters ensuring the existence of backward waves are presented. By comparison of these results, the limits of applicability of the shell theories are investigated. It is shown that the using of two-terms operator of transverse inertia is sufficient to extend the applicability of the shell theory up to high-frequency range.

articleTitle: GPR image deconvolution from antenna current waveform
abstract: This work is aimed at the improving the quality of the electromagnetic images of the subsurface medium, produced by a ground penetrating radar (GPR) where the investigated features of electrically contrast objects and interfaces are usually blurred due to inherent oscillations of the probing pulse. Parallel measurements of the aerial signal yield input data for an inverse problem allowing one to estimate the antenna current waveform and to clean up the GPR image.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic localized modes of linear periodic arrays of thin metallic wires
abstract: Electromagnetic wave modes localized along 1D periodic finite array of thin metallic parallel cylindrical wires are studied. The array is embedded into free space and excited by normally incident plane wave. We apply analysis based on the Pocklington system of integral equations to compute resonance frequencies and construct excited wave modes above the array. This approach is based on the long-wave approximation of thin wires. The description of the wave modes is directly connected with another problem of guided localized electromagnetic waves propagating along 1D periodic infinite array of thin metallic wires. For the second problem, the quasi-periodic wave field is constructed as a superposition of vector wave fields irradiated by linear electric currents. The approach is also based on the method of integral equations of Pocklington type. Dispersion curves are presented for the first lowest complex half-wave resonance of a single thin vibrator, well-known in radiophysics. An approximate quantization condition is being discussed that helps to compute resonance frequencies of the excited wave modes for the finite array. The data of the dispersion dependencies are incorporated into this quantization condition.

articleTitle: Reconstruction of solution to the wave equation from Cauchy data on the boundary
abstract: We consider the problem of determining a solution to the wave equation in Ω × ℝ (Ω ⊂ ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) from the Cauchy data given on S×I ∂Ω × ℝ. The set S ⊂ ∂Ω and the interval I ⊂ R are determined by the part of the cylinder Ω × ℝ, in which the solution is to be recovered. We provide a reconstruction algorithm based on analytical expressions.

articleTitle: Asymptotic distribution of the spectrum of symmetrically deformed unitary invariant random matrix ensemble
abstract: We study asymptotic behavior of the spectrum of some symmetric deformations of unitary invariant random matrix ensembles in the limit of infinite matrix order. We express the limiting normalized eigenvalue counting measure of an ensemble in terms of the corresponding measures of the operands by deriving functional equations for appropriate analytic transforms of the measures and compare the results obtained with the correspondent ones for other deformed ensembles.

articleTitle: Propagation of acoustic waves during the control of hydrogen-induced destruction of metals by the acoustoelastic effect
abstract: The evolution of velocities of ultrasonic waves, acoustic anisotropy and damage in the case of inelastic deformations of structures up to large plastic deformations was investigated using the method of acoustodamage. A correlation between distributions of acoustic anisotropy and distributions of hydrogen concentrations was experimentally established. Relationships between the principal values of the damage tensor and velocities of acoustic waves were obtained. The comparison of three schemes of symmetrization of the effective stress tensor in the case of inelastic uniaxial step loading of specimens from commercial alloys established that the use of implicit additive scheme gives the most conservative estimates of damage. Analysis of extreme values of the experimental angular diagrams of the acoustic anisotropy and velocities of transverse waves allowed one to define the orientation of directions of principal axes of stress tensor without unloading the structure. The results of investigation has a great importance for nondestructive acoustic control of structural elements with undefined orientation of directions of the principal axes of stress tensor.

articleTitle: Comparison of the currents in the Dirichlet and Neumann shortwave diffraction problems of a plane wave from smooth prolate bodies of revolution
abstract: This paper continues the series of works [1]-[5] on the shortwave diffraction on the prolate body of revolution. The numerical comparison of the wave currents for Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions confirms the continuous transition of the current from the lit area into the shadowed zones through Fock's zone. The formulae for the currents were obtained according to the Leontovich-Fock parabolic equation method [6]. We investigated the influence of the correction term that contains the large parameter, on the Fock's current. This large parameter reflects body's elongation. Diffraction formulae obtained in [1], [4], give the integral representation of the field in some neighborhood of the point, which is located on the boundary of geometric shadow. These formulae give a continuous transformation from ray field in the lit area to the field in the shadow using Fock's currents.

articleTitle: Current distribution and input impedance of a circular loop antenna located on the surface of a gyromagnetic cylinder
abstract: Electrodynamic characteristics of a strip loop antenna located on the surface of a gyromagnetic cylinder are studied using the integral equation method. The cylinder is aligned with the gyrotropy axis and surrounded by an isotropic magnetodielectric medium. A rigorous solution for the antenna current excited by a time-harmonic given voltage is obtained. Closed-form expressions for the current distribution and input impedance of the antenna are derived in the case of a sufficiently narrow strip.

articleTitle: High-frequency diffraction by a contour with a jump of curvature
abstract: We address high-frequency diffraction of a plane wave by a contour having a jump of curvature, aiming at explicit constructing of asymptotic formulas. In contrast to earlier research based on the Kirchhoff method, we apply a rigorous version of the boundary layer approach. Expressions for diffracted wave and wavefield in transition zone are presented.

articleTitle: Difference equations, uniform quasiclassical asymptotics and Airy functions
abstract: We consider the second order difference equation ψ(z + h) + ψ(z - h) + v(z)ψ(z) = 0 where z is a complex variable, h > 0 is a parameter, and v is an analytic function. As h → 0 the analytic solutions to this equation have quasiclassical behavior. In this note we describe their uniform asymptotics in neighborhoods of simple turning points, the neighborhoods being independent of h.

articleTitle: Breast ultrasound tomography problem, simulation with noisy model
abstract: The work is devoted to the problem of determining small sound speed fluctuations in glandular tissue for specific breast model [1], [2]. Our approach, proposed in [3],[4], is based on visualization of inclusions and unknown inner boundary between fat and glandular tissues and determination of sound speeds in inclusions using kinematic argument. In this work we examine stability of our algorithm with respect to a noise in the original breast sound speed model. We use Gaussian noise with different intensity.

articleTitle: On Morse index calculations for geodesic lines on smooth surfaces imbedded in ℝ3
abstract: Morse index appears in problems of mathematical physics devoted to construction and application of semi-classical asymptotics and short-waves propagation in inhomogeneous media, e.g. in the ray method. In this paper we present a new approach for calculation of the Morse index for geodesic lines on smooth surfaces embedded in ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>.

articleTitle: Averaged equations for bi-continuum material in the long-wavelength approximation
abstract: Fatigue failure is known to occurs in two stages. In the first stage the damage is slowly accumulated, whereas the second stage is characterised by a rapid destruction with formation of surface cracks. The hydrogen, contained both in the environment and inside the metal, reduces duration of the first stage by a hundred times. In order to describe the phenomenon of dynamic destruction, the bi-continual material model is applied. The long-wave approximation allows one to investigate the wave solutions of the equation for a slowly varying concentration amplitude of bound hydrogen, which is averaged over the period of the external load. Analysis of the dispersion relation shows that there are two different types of the wave processes depending upon the initial conditions. They are slowly decaying wave processes that model the behavior of the material at the stage of accumulation of damages, and fast developing processes that lead to destruction.

articleTitle: Fluorescence analysis of x-ray whispering gallery waves propagating along liquid meniscuses
abstract: X-ray fluorescence of whispering gallery (WG) waves, which propagate along meniscuses of silica hydrosols enriched by CsOH, has been detected and analyzed. The measurements were performed using the diffractometer with a laboratory x-ray tube at a radiation energy of 8048.05 eV, the x-ray fluorescence detector and a trough-motor system which rotates liquid samples. The WG mode propagating near the surface of a concave meniscus as well as the fluorescence intensity have been found from a solution of the respective Helmholtz equation. In order to determine the fluorescence scattering intensity, we have used the approach based on a method of fundamental parameters using the reciprocity theorem. In the analysis we used a two-layer model of the liquid surface with the upper non-uniform corrugated layer in which the concentration of levitating Cs<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> ions has a maximum near the surface, derived from the experiment, while the concentration maximum for SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> particles with sizes of ~ 10 nm is positioned at the depth of ~ 15 nm from the hydrosol surface.

articleTitle: Inverse dynamic problem for canonical systems with smooth strictly positive Hamiltonians and de Branges spaces
abstract: We solve the dynamic inverse problem for a canonical system with smooth strictly positive Hamiltonian. We also construct the corresponding de Branges space.

articleTitle: Surface waves in a polygonal domain with Robin boundary conditions
abstract: A surface wave, propagating from infinity along a semi-infinite part, interacts with the impedance boundary of a 2D polygonal domain and gives rise to the reflected surface wave on this side and to the transmitted surface wave outgoing to infinity along the second semi-infinite side of the domain. The circular outgoing wave also propagates at infinity. It is shown that the classical solution of the problem is unique. By use of some known extension of the Sommerfeld-Malyuzhinets technique the problem at hand is reduced to functional Malyuzhinets equations and then to a system of integral equations of the second kind with the integral operator depending on a characteristic parameter. The integral equations are carefully studied. From the Sommerfeld integral representation of the solution the far field asymptotics is developed.

articleTitle: Some approaches to harmonic wave propagation in elastic solids with random microstructure
abstract: We address two approaches to the problem of the one-dimensional wave propagation in elastic solids with random microstructure characterized by random elastic and mass properties. They are the method of integral spectral decomposition and the Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov equation for describing the apparatus of continuous Markov processes. Merits and deficiencies of each approach are discussed. The studied approaches are shown to cover a number of problems of the harmonic wave propagation in heterogeneous or stochastic media. Therefore by means of a preliminary analysis of a particular problem and accounting for the strong and weak side of each approach one can find an appropriate solution strategy.

articleTitle: Application of the Inverse Scattering Technique to deep water waves
abstract: We develop a method for the application of the Inverse Scattering Technique to the analysis of surface water waves and present here some evidence on its efficiency. The general idea is to interpret nonlinear wave groups in terms of soliton-type structures - envelope solitons in the framework of the integrable nonlinear Schrödinger equation. Such analysis can improve understanding of the nonlinear wave group dynamics and, in particular, could help to elaborate tools for short-term forecasting of dangerous waves in the sea. The technique may also be applied to the problem of the information decoding in soliton-based optical transmission lines.

articleTitle: Dual-tuned birdcage-like coil based on metasurfaces
abstract: We propose the dual-tuned volume coil for magnetic resonance imaging at two nuclei. This coil is based on the combination of two independent metasurfaces that can be used simultaneously for fluorine and hydrogen <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</sup>F/<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>H imaging at 7 Tesla for small animals. Each metasurface is made of nonmagnetic metallic rods and structural capacities of etched metal strips. The geometry is chosen so that two modes supported by the two metasurfaces resonate at the required frequencies 282.6/300.1 MHz. The two metasurfaces can be tuned independently by mechanically adjusting the length of the two sets of wires. We have numerically studied the concept of the proposed dual-tuned coil.

articleTitle: Differentiation of brain waves patterns in different states by multifractal analysis
abstract: We apply two methods (linear spectral analysis and nonlinear multifractal analysis) for analyzing the EEG records for experienced and inexperienced subjects, in meditation and background states. Through comparison of the obtained results, we show that the dominance of different rhythms (Lower Alpha vs. Upper Alpha) in different states for different types of subjects has a nonlinear nature. This is confirmed by the coincidence of spectral analysis and multi-fractal spectra analysis results, at least in the field where spectral analysis works. This opens new perspectives in applications of nonlinear methods for EEG time series study.

articleTitle: Coupling regimes of high-index dimer
abstract: We analyze coupling regimes in photonic structures. The simplest system composed of two high-index rods is under consideration. We derive the optical theorem for the two dimensional (2D) case, which is different from the three dimensional case. The study of scattering spectra allows us to identify three coupling regimes: strong coupling, weak coupling and a free-space coupling through Fabry-Perot resonances.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of nonlinear wave propagation in symmetric cross-ply laminates with hyperelastic material behavior
abstract: Due to microstructural damages in composite structures, for example caused by cyclic loads, material degradation may occur, changing material properties. Over time these damages are likely to accumulate and can lead to an abrupt structural failure. Therefore, it is necessary to investigate or detect material degradation as a result of cyclic loading at an early stage. For this purpose, the generation of so-called cumulative second harmonic modes [1] is employed. In this work the authors will deal with numerical simulation of Lamb-wave propagation in symmetric cross-ply laminates (CPL). Based on existing work in this area for isotropic and unidirectional materials [2], the numerical investigation is extended to CPL. The aspects of material stability as well as of conditions of existence regarding cumulative second harmonic generation in CPL will be discussed.

articleTitle: Multi-periodic one-dimensional photonic crystals
abstract: We present the results of theoretical and numerical investigation of complex one-dimensional photonic structures based on particularly ordered thin layers forming multi-periodic photonic crystals. We calculate the transmittivity spectra of electromagnetic waves for the finite-size one-dimensional multilayers (ABCD)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sup> and [(AB)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</sup> (CD)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M</sup>]<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sup>, which are single- and three-periodic one-dimensional photonic crystals composed of four different layers where N and M are the sub-period numbers and K is the super-period number. We examine the modifications of both TE- and TM-modes spectra within the first photonic band gap and its vicinity with the change of numbers N, M, K, the incidence angle θ, and the order of the layers in the structure.

articleTitle: Leaky and guided wave asymptotics in acoustics of fluid with an immersed elastic plate
abstract: The paper deals with an analytically based computer simulation of wave fields generated by a monopole source in an acoustic fluid containing an elastic plate. The explicit integral representations for generated and scattered wave fields have been derived using the Fourier transform technique. In the far-field, the body and guided waves are described by the asymptotic representations obtained from those integrals using the stationary phase method and residual technique. The asymptotics in the case of a complex pole and a stationary point approaching is presented and discussed for 2D diffraction problem. The present paper gives numerical results based on the integral and asymptotic representations at different parameters.

articleTitle: Surface spectra of discrete Laplacians
abstract: It is well known that the spectra of Laplacians on periodic graphs consist of a finite number of non-degenerate bands and eigenvalues of infinite multiplicity. We consider Laplacians on periodic graphs with boundaries. Under some conditions on the boundary the spectrum of the Laplacian has the so-called surface part, i.e., the spectrum corresponding to waves localized near the boundary. The surface spectrum is of particular interest due to its connection with the study of thermal transport, propagation of electromagnetic and acoustic waves. In this work we describe this spectrum.

articleTitle: Transformation of the modal structure of acoustical field in course of the sound propagation from continental shelf to the deep ocean
abstract: The problem of pulse signals propagation from continental shelf to the underwater sound channel of the deep sea is considered. This problem and related physical effects are important for many practical applications of underwater acoustics, including, for instance, acoustical ranging and navigation. Modal structure of acoustical field in various cross-sections of a compound waveguide consisting of a shallow- and a deep-water part is studied. Distributions of acoustical energy over the modes are computed, and the arrival times of various modal components of a pulse signal are estimated at different depths.

articleTitle: Transversal connecting orbits of Lagrangian systems with turning points: Newton–Kantorovich method
abstract: We study a natural Lagrangian system defined on a compact Riemannian manifold with potential U(q, t) = f(t)V (q). It is assumed that the factor f(t) tends to infinity as t → ±∞ and has a unique zero. It is also supposed that a set X<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>, at which V attains its maximum or minimum, consists of nondegenerate critical points. Using variational approach together with modified Newton-Kantorovich method, we establish the existence of infinitely many connecting trajectories for such a system and provide a condition for their transversality.

articleTitle: Polarization characteristics of graphene-containing composite horn antenna
abstract: The polarization characteristics of a graphene-containing composite microwave horn antenna are studied and compared with those of a similar antenna made of metal alloys. The results obtained have shown that the composite horn antenna possesses almost the same electrodynamic characteristics (amplitude-frequency response and the radiation pattern) except for the polarization ones as the conventional metal antenna. It has been established that the polarization coefficient of the composite antenna is 1.5-2 times less than that determined for the metal analog.

articleTitle: Light bullets in a planar waveguide with quadratic nonlinearity and normal group velocity dispersion
abstract: We study self-similar solutions to the second-harmonic-generation equations in a planar waveguide with transversal inhomogeneity of the refractive index, taking into account the mutual influence of quadratic nonlinearity, second-order diffraction and weak linear dispersion. Both parabolic profile and profile with saturation are investigated. It is demonstrated that waveguide geometry plays the fundamental role for spatio-temporal solitons (light bullets) existence provided that the normal dispersion is at both frequencies.

articleTitle: Isometric model of metric spaces
abstract: Let Ω be a metric space and $\mathfrak{D}$ be the lattice of its open sets with the partial order ⊆, equipped with the order topology. For a set A ⊆ Ω, let A<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</sup> denote its metric t-neighborhood. In the lattice of O-valued functions on (0, +∞), consider the family $I\mathfrak{D} = \left\{ {A\left( \cdot \right)\left| {A\left( t \right)} \right. = {A^t} \in \mathfrak{D}} \right\}$. Let $\tilde \Omega $ be the set of atoms of its closure, $\overline {I\mathfrak{D}} $, in the topology of point-wise convergence. Under certain conditions one can define a metric on $\tilde \Omega $. We describe a class of metric spaces Ω such that $\tilde \Omega $ is isometric to Ω.

articleTitle: Complex representation of general solution of equations for nonlinear model of plane deformation of crystal media with a complex lattice
abstract: Complex representation of general solution of the nonlinear equations for deformation of crystal media with a complex lattice is given for a case of plane deformation. Expressions for acoustic and optical modes, as well as for tensors of macro- and microdeformations are obtained having applied arbitrary functions of a complex variable. They are similar to the Kolosov-Muskhelishvili formulas in the presence of bulk sources. In the nonlinear model, a role of bulk sources is played by microshifts u<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> along a vector of the inverse lattice. The value u<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub> is found from the solution of a nonlinear equation of sine-Gordon type. The obtained complex representations of the general solution of the nonlinear equations allows us to apply the theory of functions of a complex variable to the solution of specific problems of the plane deformation theory.

articleTitle: Invariants and spectral estimates for Laplacians on periodic graphs
abstract: We consider Laplacians on periodic discrete graphs. The spectrum of the Laplacian consists of a finite number of bands, where degenerate bands are eigenvalues of infinite multiplicity. We introduce a new invariant I for periodic graphs and obtain a decomposition of the Laplacian into a direct integral, where fiber Laplacians (matrices) have the minimal number (≤ 2I) of coefficients depending on the quasimomentum. Using this decomposition, we estimate the position of each band and the Lebesgue measure of the Laplacian spectrum in terms of the new invariants. Moreover, similar results for Schrodinger operators with periodic potentials are obtained.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic non-polarized symmetric hybrid wave propagation in nonlinear media with saturation
abstract: The propagation of electromagnetic non-polarized symmetric hybrid waves in a planar dielectric waveguide filled with nonlinear isotropic medium with saturation is considered. The wave propagation problem is reduced to a transmission eigenvalue problem. Eigenvalues of the problem depend on an additional parameter and correspond to propagation constant. The main results of this paper are solvability theorems for the nonlinear eigenvalue problem. Numerical results are also presented.

articleTitle: Third order operator for the good Boussinesq equation on the circle
abstract: We consider a non-self-adjoint third order differential operator on R with real 1-periodic coefficients. The Lax equation for this operator is equivalent to the so-called good Boussinesq equation on the circle. The eigenvalues of the monodromy matrix constitute a 3-sheeted Riemann surface. Ramifications of this surface are invariant with respect to the Boussinesq flow. We determine high energy asymptotics of the ramifications.

articleTitle: Asymptotics of solutions to nonstationary Maxwell system in domains with small cavities
abstract: The work continues the studies of dynamic problems in singularly perturbed domains, that were initiated in [1]. The non-stationary Maxwell system is considered, for all times t ∈ ℝ, in a bounded domain with a small cavity. The impedance conditions are given on the boundary. The asymptotics of solutions are derived as the cavity diameter tends to zero. The presented mathematical model can be of use for the diagnostics of plasma filling a cavity resonator and contaminated with metal particles of small size.

articleTitle: Astigmatic Gaussian beam: Exact solution of the Helmholtz equation
abstract: Exact solution of the 3D Helmholtz equation in free space, asymptotically behaving as paraxial astigmatic Gaussian beam with no backward propagation, is presented. Construction is based on expansion in plane waves and generalizes that given in [1] for the axisymmetric case.

articleTitle: Monodromy matrices for Harper equation
abstract: We consider the Harper equation ψ(x + h) + ψ(x - h) + 2λ cos (2πx)ψ(x) = Eψ(x), x ℝ, where h > 0, 0 <; λ ≤ 1, and E ∈ ℝ are parameters. This equation appears as a model in solid state physics and has intriguing spectral properties. In the quasiclassical limit, i.e., as h → 0, we describe the asymptotics of monodromy matrices for the Harper equation. This enables us to get information on the asymptotic structure of the spectrum.

articleTitle: Fuchsian Heun equation, equivalent Fuchsian linear systems and Painlevé PVI equation
abstract: Famous Painlevé VI equation is connected with the linear differential equations of Fuchsian type by different links. Nevertheless, there is a common point. It is the Hamiltonian nature of the Painlevé equation. We demonstrate how the different normalizations draw us to the different approaches to the problem.

articleTitle: Low frequency spectra of layered plates and their parametrical study
abstract: New method based on the combination of asymptotic and numerical approaches is suggested for evaluating the total infinite set of dispersion curves. The long wave asymptotics for the complex dispersion curves are derived. It is proved that each dispersion curve has a flat segment at low frequency. The exact complex curves are calculated together with fundamental modes and their possible pure imaginary "sisters". The influence of the geometrical and elastic parameters is studied.

articleTitle: Semi-analytical hybrid approach for modelling wave motion excited by a piezoelectric transducer in periodic layered composite with a crack
abstract: The paper presents a semi-analytical hybrid approach for modelling the interaction of a piezoelectric transducer and with a periodic elastic structure with a crack. It combines advantages of the frequency domain spectral element method using Gauss-Legendre-Lobatto polynomials and the boundary integral approach. The unknown crack-opening-displacement and the traction vector in the contact area are determined via Galerkin method.

articleTitle: Modelling of damaged interface dynamic behaviour via random and periodic crack distributions
abstract: Models of the imperfect interface assuming a random distribution of rectangular micro-cracks are presented. Numerical solution of the boundary integral equation for a single crack is required for estimating the spring stiffnesses. Asymptotic representation for the kernel of the integral equation allows deriving analytical expressions for the displacement jump. Comparison of normal and tangential components of stiffnesses matrix is made for random distributions of square and circular cracks. A damaged interface is also modelled by a doubly periodic array of square or rectangular defects.

articleTitle: Theoretical and experimental study of diffraction by a thin cone
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: elasticity; eigenvalues and eigenfunctions; wave propagation; integral equations; nonlinear differential equations; Schrodinger equation; elastic waves; photonic crystals; Helmholtz equations; electromagnetic wave propagation.

articleTitle: Ice-coupled surface water waves near a vertical barrier
abstract: Exact analytical solution is provided for the scattering of incident flexural-gravity waves in water of a finite depth against a junction of a floating elastic plate with a vertical slope of a hydraulic structure. The floating plate is considered to be attached with the vertical barrier in different ways, giving rise to edge conditions: free edge, clamped edge, sliding edge, and sliding with friction edge conditions. Important physical quantities such as bending moment, shear force and vertical displacement of the plate are determined. Approximations of infinitely deep fluid and a thin fluid layer are also under consideration.

articleTitle: Numerical solution of iterative parabolic equations approximating the nonlinear Helmholtz equation
abstract: Recently a new approach to the modeling of one-way wave propagation in Kerr media was proposed [1]. Within this approach the solution of the nonlinear Helmholtz equation is approximated by a series of solutions of iterative parabolic equations (IPEs). It was also shown that IPEs take the nonparaxial propagation effects into account. In this study we develop an efficient pseudospectral numerical method for solving the system of IPEs. The method is a generalization of an exponential time differencing (ETD) method for the nonlinear Schrödinger equation [2]. The ETD technique is well-suited for the system of IPEs, as it allows to reduce the order of the derivative in the input term.

articleTitle: Purcell effect in a disordered photonic crystals
abstract: We consider the one-dimensional problem of imperfections' influence on the Purcell effect in photonic crystal system. We demonstrate that the presence of disorder in a one-dimensional photonic crystal can lead to a modification of the spontaneous emission rate in the photonic band gap (PBG) frequency region. We show that the amount of disorder regulates two different scenarios of the Purcell effect modification. In the case of weak disorder, the Purcell enhancement of the spontaneous emission occurs at PBG edges, and, in the case of strong disorder, it occurs at PBG centre.

articleTitle: Noncollinear interaction features of optical waves with wide spectrum in nonlinear dielectric medium
abstract: We perform the numerical studies of non-collinear interaction of few-cycle waves in a medium with a significant linear dispersion and an instantaneous third-order nonlinearity. We show that such an interaction can lead to generation of sum-frequency radiation which propagates in a new direction.

articleTitle: Tunable metasurface composed of periodic metal-dielectric resonators
abstract: Observation of the wanted Raman signal from SERS substrates is hampered by the background luminescence. We investigate the metasurface made of periodic silicon micro bars with thin silver layer on the top. The computer simulations as well as real experiment reveal the anomalous optical response of the metasurface is due to the excitation of the metal-dielectric surface resonances. We demonstrate the enhanced Raman signal from the organic molecules of 5,5-dithio-bis[2-nitrobenzoic] acid deposited on the microbar metasurface. The microbar metasurface exhibits large Raman/luminescence (signal/noise) ratio. As result it operates as an efficient SERS substrate.

articleTitle: Interaction of nonsymmetric electromagnetic waves guided by cylindrical duct with enhanced density in magnetoactive plasma
abstract: The nonlinear interaction of nonsymmetric electromagnetic waves guided by cylindrical duct with enhanced plasma density in magnetoactive plasma has been considered. The parametric instability of the nonsymmetric electromagnetic guided waves propagating in the opposite directions is analyzed in the case of the cylinder filled with a resonant magnetoactive plasma. For the some practically interesting cases, analytical and numerical results illustrating the interaction of the guided waves are presented.

articleTitle: Propagation of electromagnetic waves in a shielded dielectric layer with cubic nonlinearity
abstract: An eigenvalue problem describing propagation of transverse magnetic waves in a shielded dielectric layer with cubic nonlinearity is studied. It is proved that even for small value of the nonlinearity coefficient, the nonlinear problem has infinitely many nonperturbative solutions (eigenvalues and eigenfunctions), whereas the corresponding linear problem always has a finite number of solutions.

articleTitle: Theoretical and experimental study of resonance Lamb wave scattering by an impact-induced damage in an isotropic multi-layered plate
abstract: Resonance interaction of elastic guided waves with a stack of planar three-dimensional delaminations in an isotropic laminate structure is investigated. Eigenfrequencies and eigenforms of the diffraction problem considered are analyzed relying on the analytically- and mesh-based computational models. An approach for experimental resonance frequency extraction from B-scan and point-wise measurements with scanning laser Doppler vibrometry is proposed and implemented. A good agreement between predicted and measured eigenfrequencies and corresponding localization patterns (eigenforms) is observed.

articleTitle: Spheroidal model based on the quasistatic approximation
abstract: We suggest an approximate approach to solution of the light scattering problem for an axisymmetric particle. The approach includes the replacement of the scatterer by a spheroid and use of the quasistatic approximation. Applicability of the approach is numerically considered in the case of finite cylinders. It is found that the approach can be useful in a wide range of parameter values, and it is in particular appropriate to optically soft scatterers of large eccentricity.

articleTitle: The spectral functions method for elastic plane wave diffraction by a wedge
abstract: Non destructive examination of industrial structures requires the modeling of specimen geometry echoes generated by the surfaces (entry, back-wall, etc.) of inspected blocks. For that purpose, the study of plane elastic wave diffraction by a wedge is of great interest since surfaces of complex industrial specimen often include dihedral corners. These inspections often deal with high frequency (f = 2-5 MHz) ultrasonic waves. Simulation of realistic inspections by finite elements and finite differences can therefore be time consuming because such methods require a small mesh step for a better description of the scattered wave. Semi-analytical methods are therefore preferred for high frequency problems. There exist various approaches for semi-analytical modeling of plane elastic wave diffraction by a wedge but the theoretical and numerical aspects of these methods have so far only been developed for wedge angles lower than π. Croisille and Lebeau [1] have introduced a resolution method called the Spectral Functions method in the different case of an immersed elastic wedge of angle less than π. Kamotski and Lebeau [2] have then proven existence and uniqueness of the solution derived from this method to the diffraction problem of stress-free wedges embedded in an elastic medium. The advantages of this method are its validity for wedge angles greater than π and its adaptability to more complex cases. The methodology of Croisille and Lebeau [1] has been first extended by the authors to the simpler case of an immersed soft wedge [3] (submitted). It has then been developed here for the 2D scattering problem of an elastic longitudinal wave and a numerical validation of the method for all wedge angles is proposed.

articleTitle: Semi-classical Green functions
abstract: Let H(x, p) ~ H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>(x, p) + hH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>(x, p) + ... be a semi-classical Hamiltonian on T*R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>, and Σ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">E</sub> = {H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>(x, p) = E} be a non-critical energy surface. Consider f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">h</sub>, a semi-classical distribution (the "source") microlocalized on a Lagrangian manifold Λ which intersects cleanly the flow-out Λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sub> of the Hamilton vector field XH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> in Σ. Using Maslov's canonical operator, we look for a semi-classical distribution u<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">h</sub> satisfying the limiting absorption principle and H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">w</sup>(x, hD<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>)u<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">h</sub> = f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">h</sub> (semi-classical Green function). In this report, we elaborate (still at an early stage) on some results announced in [1] and provide some examples, in particular, from the theory of wave beams.
